physicalNotes: Radius 0.6489 +/- 0.0013 solar radii, mass 0.6897 (+0.0035/-0.0034) solar masses and effective temperature 4450 +/- 150 K from Doyle et al. (2011, Science 333, 1602; arXiv:1109.3432), Table 1, the photometric-dynamical model of the Kepler light curve and the radial velocities of star A: 451,439.73 km at 695,700 km per solar radius; GM is the mass times the JPL solar GM 132712440041.93938 km^3/s^2. Sebastian et al. (2025, MNRAS; arXiv:2505.19718) measure dynamical masses 2-7% higher with SOPHIE; they are not mixed into this record because Doyle's orbits were fitted with Doyle's masses. presentationUp: no spin axis is measured, so the display axis (celestial north at the star) is up.

sources.position: SIMBAD basic record for Kepler-16 (Gaia DR3 2133476355197071616), ICRS J2000 position, reference 2020yCat.1350....0G, retrieved 2026-09-23. Gaia sees the unresolved pair; star B adds 1.5% of the Kepler-band light (flux ratio 0.01555, Doyle et al. 2011, Table 1), so the photocentre is star A to well under a milliarcsecond.
sources.distance: Gaia EDR3 parallax 13.2806 +/- 0.0284 mas via SIMBAD (2020yCat.1350....0G): 75.30 pc, no zero-point correction
sources.radialVelocity: The radial velocity of the barycentre, gamma = -32.769 +/- 0.035 km/s, Doyle et al. (2011, Science 333, 1602; arXiv:1109.3432), Table 1. Star A's own orbital motion about the barycentre is carried by the hosted orbits, not by this catalogue velocity.
